callouts.title: Double-Mindedness Is the Spiritual Dilemma
callouts.text: Alma warned the people of Gideon against the "awful dilemma" of their brethren in Zarahemla. The footnote points to James 1:8 — "A double minded man is unstable in all his ways." This instability comes from divided loyalty between God and worldly priorities.

callouts.title: God's Pattern: Firstlings First
callouts.text: From Adam and Eve onward, the Lord commanded His children to offer the firstlings of their flocks — giving Him the first and best, not leftovers. This pattern existed from the beginning to prevent double-mindedness and point to Christ's sacrifice.

callouts.title: Windows of Heaven = Spiritual Illumination
callouts.text: Malachi's promise to open the "windows of heaven" is not just temporal blessings. Elder Bednar taught: windows allow natural light to enter. Spiritual illumination and perspective are poured out as we honor the law of tithing — this is enhanced spiritual capacity.

callouts.title: Jesus Christ Put the Father First
callouts.text: The Savior is the perfect example of putting God first. He laid down His life as a symbol of complete submission to His Father's will. When we pay tithing, we follow His pattern of obedience and sacrifice, inviting the Holy Ghost into our lives as He did for Adam (Moses 5:9).

threads.title: Question 1: What is the "awful dilemma" Alma warned about?

qa_pairs.question: What did Alma identify as the spiritual dilemma facing the people of Zarahemla?
qa_pairs.answer: Alma described an "awful dilemma" and "state of dilemma" that the people of Zarahemla were in. The footnote in Alma 7:18 points to James 1:8: "A double minded man is unstable in all his ways." This dilemma is double-mindedness — being wavering, indecisive, or conflicted, lacking commitment to a single purpose or belief. It's the instability that comes from trying to serve both God and mammon.

qa_pairs.question: How does double-mindedness manifest in our lives today?
qa_pairs.answer: Double-mindedness appears when we compartmentalize our faith — keeping God in a Sunday box while making daily decisions based on worldly priorities. It's the hesitation to fully trust God with our finances, time, or future because we want a backup plan. Elder Becerra's experience shows it as falling behind in tithing while trying to grow a business "his way" instead of God's way.

threads.title: Question 2: How does putting God first overcome double-mindedness?

qa_pairs.question: What did Jesus teach as the remedy for divided loyalty?
qa_pairs.answer: Jesus taught: "Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness." Putting God first is the antidote to double-mindedness because it establishes a single, supreme priority. When God is genuinely first, every other decision flows from that center — there's no competition for first place.

qa_pairs.question: What does it practically look like to "seek first" in daily decisions?
qa_pairs.answer: It means evaluating every choice — financial, relational, temporal — through the lens: "Does this put God first?" For Elder Becerra, it meant selling his only car (his business asset) to pay tithing. For us, it might mean paying tithing before the mortgage, serving a calling when busy, or choosing Sabbath observance over overtime. The pattern: identify what you value most, and offer it to God first.

threads.title: Question 3: Why did the Lord command Adam and Eve to offer firstlings?

qa_pairs.question: What was the purpose of the firstlings commandment given to Adam and Eve?
qa_pairs.answer: The Lord commanded Adam and Eve to "worship the Lord their God, and should offer the firstlings of their flocks." Adam obeyed even before understanding why. An angel later revealed: "This thing is a similitude of the sacrifice of the Only Begotten of the Father, which is full of grace and truth." The firstlings were a type of Christ — giving the first and best pointed to the Father giving His Firstborn Son.

qa_pairs.question: Why "firstlings" specifically — why not just any offering?
qa_pairs.answer: Firstlings represent the best, the prime, the irreplaceable. Offering leftovers costs nothing; offering firstlings costs trust. The pattern from Eden establishes that God doesn't want our surplus — He wants our first and best, which requires faith that He will provide the rest. This prevents double-mindedness by forcing a choice: trust God with the first, or keep it for security.

threads.title: Question 4: What does Elder Becerra's car experience teach about tithing?

qa_pairs.question: How did Elder Becerra's experience with selling his car demonstrate the principle of firstlings?
qa_pairs.answer: As a young father behind on tithing, Elder Becerra was asked by Elder Cutler: "Do you have anything of value?" His only asset was his business car. After pondering, he sold it for the exact amount needed to pay off the loan AND his tithing — no haggling. Days later, a friend offered him another car when he had none. He gave his "firstling" (only car), and the Lord provided.

qa_pairs.question: Did Elder Cutler tell him to sell the car?
qa_pairs.answer: No. Elder Becerra explicitly states: "I want to be clear that Elder Cutler did not ask me to sell my car. This came to me after pondering and desiring to put God first." The decision came from his own desire to obey, not external pressure. This mirrors Adam — Adam obeyed before understanding; Elder Becerra acted on faith, then received understanding through the miracle that followed.

threads.title: Question 5: How do a mother's testimony and President Hinckley's promise reinforce tithing?

qa_pairs.question: What did Elder Becerra's mother testify during a home evening lesson?
qa_pairs.answer: Despite financial setbacks as immigrants, she said with "a gaze of her certain witness": "All we need to see is the very hand of Jehovah Himself to have any greater assurance that He is blessing us by our payment of tithing." Her testimony wasn't theoretical — it was forged in the same financial pressure Elder Becerra faced, making it a generational anchor.

qa_pairs.question: What did President Hinckley promise about tithing and poverty?
qa_pairs.answer: "I believe they will not walk out of poverty unless they pay their tithing... It is obedience to the commandment of the Lord that really matters." (General Authority training, Oct. 2, 2001). Elder Becerra notes this applies to spiritual poverty too — we don't walk out of spiritual darkness without the obedience of tithing. The principle: obedience opens the windows of heaven for both temporal and spiritual deliverance.

threads.title: Question 6: What spiritual capacity comes through tithing obedience?

qa_pairs.question: What happened after Adam offered sacrifice in obedience?
qa_pairs.answer: "And in that day the Holy Ghost fell upon Adam." The sequence is clear: commandment → obedience (firstlings) → sacrifice → Holy Ghost. Elder Bednar connects this to Malachi's windows: spiritual illumination pours in as we honor tithing. The "enhanced spiritual capacity" Elder Becerra promises is the companionship and direction of the Holy Ghost.

qa_pairs.question: How does tithing enhance our spiritual capacity in practical terms?
qa_pairs.answer: Spiritual capacity means: clearer revelation for decisions, stronger resistance to temptation, greater capacity to love and serve, peace amid uncertainty, and the ability to discern God's hand in daily life. Elder Bednar's "windows" metaphor: just as windows bring natural light to illuminate a room, tithing opens heaven's windows to illuminate our path. The Holy Ghost becomes our constant companion, not an occasional visitor.

What blessings have you seen in your life through keeping the law of tithing, even when it was hard?

How do you offer 'the firstlings of [your] flock' (Moses 5:5) to the Lord in your current circumstances?
